rubrics.justification: Description is consistent with a very poor-quality early blastocyst/1DD, noting poorly defined blastocoel, absent/degenerative ICM, sparse irregular TE, and no hatching. Minor limitation is some image-dependent uncertainty and a few inferred features like coarse/granular degeneration.

Thoroughly integrates maternal age, ovarian reserve, BMI, prior IVF outcomes, endometrial thickness, partner age, sperm parameters, and lifestyle, and clearly explains how these modify prognosis relative to the poor embryo morphology.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent: poor ICM/TE and day-5 developmental weakness drive low implantation odds, while favorable lining and prior live birth modestly temper but do not override the prognosis.

Generally aligned with Gardner grading principles and standard IVF counseling: poor-quality blastocyst has low priority, SET is appropriate, bed rest/add-ons are not recommended, and PGT-A is discussed cautiously. Slight deduction because exact implantation percentages for 1DD are not guideline-based and some suggestions are more expert-opinion than formal guideline.

Provides clear next steps for current transfer and future planning, including counseling if this is the only embryo, prioritization against better embryos, review of recurrent embryo-quality issues, protocol reassessment, PGT-A discussion, sperm DNA fragmentation workup, uterine cavity review, and lifestyle optimization.
